stories.title: Spy scandal / Hegseth’s future / Are we still at war with Iran?
stories.description: An American tech giant in the arms of an alleged Chinese spy. Now, Jensen Huang and Nvidia are at the center of a national security crisis.Host Mary Louise Kelly talks to National Security Correspondent Greg Myre and Pentagon Correspondent Tom Bowman about what the scandal could mean for the AI race and what was the world's largest company. And they discuss where the Iran war stands after this week's failed attempt to impeach Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth.A note to listeners: a few weeks ago, Mary Louise announced that she is stepping down from her role as host of NPR’s All Things Considered and Sources & Methods to pursue new adventures. She’ll still be a contributor to NPR, but no longer a host. Thank you for spending these past 15 months with us.We don’t know what the future holds. stories.title: Parrots' vibrant feathers are surprisingly susceptible to bacterial attack
stories.description: Flashy birds, from peacocks to parrots, have inspired a long tradition of using animal colors to study evolution. Colorful plumage often functions as a signal—for example, to attract a mate. Alternatively, drab colors can be used for camouflage. However, color can have functions beyond signaling and camouflage. This is because pigments, the molecules embedded in feather tissues to produce a broad range of colors, can also influence other aspects of feathers, ranging from mechanical strength to thermoregulatory properties.

stories.title: A surprising brain difference may explain why some kids struggle with math
stories.description: Stanford researchers have discovered that children who struggle persistently with math may have underlying differences in how their brains manage problem-solving strategies. Children with developmental dyscalculia were slower to switch strategies, less responsive to changes in difficulty, and less able to improve their approach over time. Distinct patterns of brain activity were linked to these difficulties and could even predict certain math-related abilities.
